title: Rabbit at Tom Anderson's cabaret: Downfall of the Lion and Gypsy Blood
summary: Nash recalls Rabbit singing his made-up topical songs at Tom Anderson's cabaret, including one on the killing of the police chief (David Hennessy) and another about the Gypsy Blood murders on Franklin Street.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Here's some more. Where did Rabbit sing Downfall of the Lion?

Yeah, the Tom Anderson Cabaret. He hung around there, huh? Yeah, he used to come in there and sing all those numbers he made up. And he made up another song about Gypsy Blood, the time they had all that killing down there. He had several little songs right there.
You mean Billy Phillips and that Parker fella that got killed?
Yeah, what he said about the killer of the chief, way back down years ago.
What about Gypsy Blood? What was that?

There was a lot of murdering that happened down there in the quarters. I think that happened somewhere around Tom Anderson up in there somewhere. That happened. But I was so young, I just can't remember. Anyhow Rabbit used to go around and sing a song about downfall, that was the downfall of the lion. I think when the chief of police got killed. That's David Hennessy.
Yeah, yeah. But Gypsy Blood was a different thing. Yeah.
That was on Franklin Street. Somewhere. I just can't remember it so good. Yeah. But that's way back.
